clue.text: Where one gets to writing keenly at first in the USSR

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase of place: a city found in the Soviet Union

parts.note: taken as written
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word keenly

explanation.surface: Someone writing eagerly about where they will end up in the Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomsk is a Siberian city, part of the Soviet Union when this puzzle was set.

clue.text: Excellent cricket score, say

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine innings in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: A notch was once a cut on a tally stick recording a run, so the top notch is the highest score.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate quality; and, read literally, the highest scoring mark cut on a cricket tally stick.

clue.text: Being low, dear, in France skulking around

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing activity, while the answer names the person doing it

parts.note: a cow lowing says moo
cher is French for dear

explanation.surface: Someone feeling depressed while hanging about in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being low' suggests sadness, but it is the sound of cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A moocher is a loiterer who idles or slinks about aimlessly.

clue.text: Short measure

parts.note: suggests a stingy serving at the bar, but means a unit of measurement given in shortened form

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the usual clipped form of kilogram or kilometre, both units of measurement.

clue.text: Biblical character with a broken harp I observe

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of harp and I are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
to observe something is to see it

explanation.surface: Picturing a figure from scripture spotted holding a damaged harp.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a strict Jewish sect, often appearing in the Gospels as opponents of Jesus.

clue.text: Re-knit better wool that it may be used for warmth

definitions.text: it may be used for warmth

indicators.note: reknitting wool unpicks it and remakes it, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to knit some good wool again into something cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Re-knit' rearranges the fourteen letters of BETTER WOOL THAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber container filled from the kettle and tucked into bed to keep someone warm.

clue.text: Spellbound in rewritten part

indicators.note: rewriting the word part puts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: An actor enthralled by a newly revised role.
explanation.definitionFit: Entranced and wholly absorbed, as if under a spell.

clue.text: He tries to find a way to under write currency

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece is written under the first

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a river is something with a current, a currency

explanation.surface: Someone working hard to underwrite a nation's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like money, but is read as a thing that has a current.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who makes great efforts, someone who keeps trying.

clue.text: Clear air thereabout

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or moved about, so the letters of there are rearranged

explanation.surface: Weather report of a clear sky in that area.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic word for the upper sky, the clear heavens above the clouds.

clue.text: Sharp practice could leave him with a sore throat

definitions.text: Sharp practice could leave him with a sore throat

parts.words: Sharp practice could leave him with a sore throat
parts.note: sharp practice usually means dishonesty, but here it is rehearsing with blades that go down the throat

explanation.definitionFit: A fairground performer who pushes a blade down into the gullet.

clue.text: Clearly not one for the rich

definitions.text: Clearly not one for the rich

parts.words: Clearly not one for the rich
parts.note: a piece of legislation that obviously applied to the needy rather than the wealthy

explanation.definitionFit: Old English statutes governing relief for paupers through parish workhouses.

clue.text: Ruler who has to dry up

parts.note: taken as written
to parch is to dry out

explanation.surface: A monarch obliged to dry out.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for the governor of a small state or city.

clue.text: Emperor found in the hot-house

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words the hot-house

explanation.surface: A ruler discovered lurking in the greenhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman who ruled briefly in AD 69, the Year of the Four Emperors.

clue.text: Distress signal from George on a horse

indicators.note: on places the first piece before the second in an across answer

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for the name George
a roan is a horse with a mixed-colour coat

explanation.surface: A rider called George sends out an alarm from horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A low moan, a sound expressing pain or misery.

clue.text: One very cut off town in Bucks

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: cut off removes the tail letter of the word very

explanation.surface: A lone very isolated place in the English countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Bucks is Buckinghamshire, a county west of London; Iver is a village there.
explanation.definitionFit: A settlement in south Buckinghamshire near Slough, home to Pinewood film studios.

clue.text: Be an angel, you brute!

parts.note: taken as written
an, an article, gives A
ST is the abbreviation for saint, taken here as an angel

explanation.surface: A pleading 'be nice' followed by an insult.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface swings from flattery to abuse; the angel is a saint, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse or savage person, an animal in human form.

clue.text: Flood caused by turning taps with energy

indicators.note: turning a word round reads its letters backwards

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A torrent released by vigorously turning on the taps.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden rush of water, as when a river rises fast.

clue.text: As precepts were devised for cleaners

indicators.note: devised means worked out afresh, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Household rules drawn up for the domestic staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Manual devices with rotating brushes, pushed over rugs to pick up dust.

clue.text: Frightful creature taking a fielding position on my right

parts.note: taken as written
mid-on is a fielding position in cricket, near the bowler on the leg side

explanation.surface: A monster stationed on the cricket field to my right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... on' tells you the fielding position follows MY R.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired thug or henchman, named after Achilles' warlike followers.

clue.text: Tiers of layers along the shore for protection?

parts.note: coastal means situated by the seashore
a battery is a set of stacked cages for egg-laying hens

explanation.surface: Rows of hens kept by the seaside for their safety.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layers' looks like strata; they are egg-laying hens, kept in a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of heavy guns sited on the seaboard to defend against ships.

clue.text: Makes me reflexive, speaking regally

parts.note: a monarch using the royal we needs a singular reflexive pronoun in place of myself

explanation.definitionFit: The royal form of myself, used by a sovereign speaking in the plural.

clue.text: Butler's ideal nowhere to be found

indicators.note: the letters of nowhere must be worked out, found in a new order

explanation.surface: A manservant's perfect world proves impossible to locate.
explanation.walkthrough: Butler is Samuel Butler, whose satirical novel's imaginary land rearranges 'nowhere'.
explanation.definitionFit: The utopian land of Samuel Butler's 1872 satire.

clue.text: Yorkshire banker with a keen resentment

parts.note: ire is sharp anger

explanation.surface: A bitter financier in the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, which has banks; the Aire flows through Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A river of West Yorkshire.

clue.text: I join up with Father coming back, and get support

indicators.note: coming back reads the whole run of pieces backwards in this down light

parts.note: taken as written
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A child joins Dad on his return and gets help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns I + UP + PA into APPUI.
explanation.definitionFit: A military and fencing term for a prop or point of backing.

clue.text: Arboreal deadly sinner?

parts.note: a tree-dwelling creature that shares its name with one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.definitionFit: A slow tree-hanging South American mammal, also the sin of idleness.

clue.text: Crack from a seaman not articled

indicators.note: not articled means the article an is taken out of the word seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor without an apprenticeship cracking under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articled' suggests a trainee clerk; here it means having an article (AN) in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow opening or line where two things join, or a rock fissure.

clue.text: No-one's up in the Swiss town

indicators.note: up in a down light reads the letters from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, and 's adds S

explanation.surface: Nobody is awake in an Alpine town.
explanation.definitionFit: Sion is the capital of the canton of Valais in Switzerland.

clue.text: An aching for French bread

explanation.surface: Longing for a baguette.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurt or ache; and the French word for a loaf.

clue.text: Quietly criticise the show in advance

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to review a work is to criticise it

explanation.surface: A critic quietly panning a production before it opens.
explanation.definitionFit: A showing to an audience before the official opening.

clue.text: Felt strongly carrying the burden around

indicators.note: carrying here means one word holds another within it
around confirms that the word burden goes about the word the

parts.note: a load is a burden
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone resentful while carrying a heavy weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Detested, held an intense dislike for.

clue.text: What's afoot in the Forces

parts.note: what's going on in the services, reread as the troops who go on foot

explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers, the army's walking troops.

clue.text: No inn? Strange -that's a fabrication!

indicators.note: strange signals the letters of no inn are made into something odd

explanation.surface: A traveller finding no inn suspects a lie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fabrication' looks like a lie but means a fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A light sheer silk or rayon material.
